description: A single, high-confidence P1 security finding (missing authorization check) with every other reviewer clean.

findings.title: Missing authorization check on workspace deletion endpoint
findings.description: The new `DELETE /api/workspaces/:id` handler deletes the workspace after only verifying the caller is authenticated, never checking that the caller is a member (let alone an owner) of that workspace. Any authenticated user can delete any workspace by id.
findings.recommendation: Verify the caller has an owner-level `WorkspaceMembership` for the target workspace before deleting it.

reviewer_runs.summary: Existing tests don't cover authorization for this new endpoint, but that follows from the missing check itself.

expected.rationale: A confirmed, high-confidence P1 broken-access-control finding lets any authenticated user destroy any workspace. This is a realistic, severe, immediately-exploitable security defect — the kind of confirmed P1 security finding the judge should treat as release-blocking on its own, independent of what any other reviewer reported.

explanation: Tests the judge's own policy judgment: a single confirmed, severe security P1 should block release even though the deterministic floor alone (minimumVerdictFor) only guarantees APPROVE_WITH_MINOR_FIXES for one P1 — a well-tuned judge is expected to be stricter than the bare floor here, not merely as strict as it.
